$comment: The record properties SecurityInsight WRITES ITSELF (not what a source offers). Continuous discovery sees them on the records like any other property, so this list keeps them off Configuration > New context available: they are recorded as known (Everything known), never as new context. THE RULE (owner 2026-11-25: 'if we control it, why dont you fill out these fields and activate them'): every property SecurityInsight writes ships in the same release either MAPPED to the si_ field(s) named here (use 'mapped', the shipped field map reads it) or listed as INTERNAL ('internal', with why). A test holds it: every entry is mapped or internal-with-a-reason, every mapped entry is read by the shipped field map, and every part the privilege tier classifier writes is listed. property: the property as discovery names it inside the part ('key', 'key.child'); a trailing * matches every property that starts with the text before it. recordTypes: '*' = every record type of the source. The web app reads an embedded copy (pro-management/src/SI.Management.Core/ProData/DataModel), held to this file by a test.

properties.why: the object that holds the level inside Tier 0; its parts below are mapped or listed one by one
the level inside Tier 0: 1 = a Tier 0 role held tenant-wide, 2 = every Tier 0 role held on a scope only
why the identity is Tier 0, in words: the deciding role and, for a scoped role, the scope's type, name and id
always 0 -- the level is written only for a Tier 0 identity; the identity's tier itself is si_privilege_tier_permanent / si_privilege_tier_eligible

the deciding scoped roles behind the text: the text names them (role, scope type, name and id), every scoped assignment is in si_entra_role_scopes and the group a role is held through in si_role_paths
the install tag on the resource group of a SecurityInsight install: it says which install a resource belongs to, not context about the customer's own resources
SecurityInsight's own tags on its own resources (what is installed, the updater's record, its components)
Invardia's install tags on the resources of a SecurityInsight install
